newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: SFE wheat rises as El Nino scare grips market.
newsitem.headline: SFE wheat rises as El Nino scare grips market.

text.p: Sydney Futures Exchange (SFE) wheat futures rose strongly in active trading as El Nino drought fears gripped the market.
The January and March 1998 contracts both traded up by A$5.50 a tonne, to A$187.00 and A$189.50 a tonne respectively. A total of 36 lots changed hands.

The rising market also produced interest in January 1998 call options, with two lots of A$185.00 selling at A$11.50, four lots of A$190.00 selling at A$8.00 and two lots of A$200.00 selling at A$6.00.
"The El Nino drought scare is starting to bite," Phil Lindsay of Ord Minnett Jardine Fleming Futures said.

Stories were circulating on Monday that New South Wales growers had begun turning sheep onto their wheat crops because of fear of a failed season. Also in Western Australia only 10 percent germination had occurred so far, raising fears that production would be substantially down on last year, he said.
Monday's rise intensified market reaction to El Nino fears which began to strike last weeek.
Australian wheat futures could rise to A$240.00 a tonne in a fully-blown drought, Lindsay said.
